newsitem.title: BURMA: Thousands rally in support of Burma military.
newsitem.headline: Thousands rally in support of Burma military.

text.p: About 35,000 members of a Burmese government-backed group rallied in northern Mandalay and denounced opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi for calling for sanctions on Burma, official media reported on Monday.

"The Bogadaw (wife of British citizen) wrote repeatedly to external puppet masters to impose sanctions on Myanmar (Burma) and not to allow Myanmar's entry into ASEAN," the media quoted the chairman of the rally, U Tin Maung Oo, as saying at the rally on Sunday.
Suu Kyi, who heads the opposition National League for Democracy, is married to a British academic.

The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam and Brunei. Burma, Laos and Cambodia are expected to be invited to join the group later this year.

The rally, held by the United Solidarity and Development Organisation (USDA), praised the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), but denounced "the destructive acts of internal and external subversive elements", the media reported.
"The U.S. government is acting as the world police to apply hegemonism and their American First neo-colonialist policy to control the world," said another USDA executive, Ma S Zawng Naw.

The United States imposed economic sanctions on Burma in April, banning new investment by American firms, as a condemnation of the Burmese military junta's alleged human rights abuses and suppression of Suu Kyi's pro-democracy movement.
Suu Kyi praised Washington for imposing the latest sanctions and has been at odds with ASEAN over its plan to include Burma in its grouping.
Analysts in Rangoon said similar rallies by USDA members would take place in other cities in coming weeks.
